narrative:
Your loan application was denied because our model predicts an 84% chance that you represent a bad credit risk, based on details like your 60-month loan duration, 6836 DM credit amount, business purpose, checking account with less than 0 DM, and history of past payment delays. These factors together signal higher risk to the model, especially since your requested amount is more than double the average of about 2887 DM for approved applicants, and your duration far exceeds their typical 19 months. In contrast, approved applicants more often have shorter terms, smaller loans for everyday needs like cars or appliances, cleaner credit histories such as fully paid credits, and checking balances at least at 0 DM or better.

To understand why, we looked at "what if" scenarios—counterfactuals—that show the minimal changes needed to flip the model's decision from denial to approval. We generated three such scenarios, and in every single one, three key factors always changed together: shortening your loan duration from 60 to 24 months, switching the purpose from business to buying a used car, and reducing the credit amount from 6836 DM to around 2957 DM. No other aspects of your profile—like your long employment of over 7 years, skilled job, own housing, or lack of other installment plans—needed to budge; they stayed exactly as they are and were deemed fine by the model.

These three features changed in 100% of the scenarios, with duration dropping by an average of 36 months, the purpose shifting unanimously to used car, and the amount decreasing by about 3879 DM on average—putting you squarely in line with approved applicants' norms. The other 14 features, including your savings under 100 DM (common even among approvals at 55.6%) and two existing credits (slightly above their average of 1.42), never changed at all, showing they weren't the main roadblocks.

Realistically, you could improve your odds by requesting a shorter 24-month term instead of 60, aiming for a used car purchase rather than business needs (which only make up 9.3% of approvals), and scaling back to roughly 3000 DM—changes that align with what typically gets approved without altering your stable employment or residence history. These adjustments would likely tip the prediction to good credit, as they directly address the model's biggest concerns in your case. Keep in mind that in 1970s Germany, with average salaries around 10,000-20,000 DM, smaller, shorter loans for practical purposes were standard for approvals.
